specification.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

execution.description: Positive control: reads the command tag of PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT, reports a COMMIT error as a failure, and discards a connection whose ROLLBACK failed. It starts a transaction at the isolation level requested of it.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

api_outcome.contract: The correct control runs a migration in one transaction. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock before it reads history, applies the migration only when history has no entry, and commits the marker and the history entry together. A reversal deletes the marker and the history entry, refuses a migration that has no reversal, and rolls back a reversal that raises.
